summary: Fixed null crmProfileId crash in disposition writers. In distribute/route.ts (lines 98-112) replaced `crmProfileId!` with a spread conditional that omits the disposition op entirely when crmProfileId is null, preventing the non-null assertion from throwing inside the transaction and rolling back the whole round-robin distribute. In redistribute/route.ts (lines 87-105) wrapped the audit insert in an `if (session.user.crmProfileId)` guard plus a try/catch that logs but does not rethrow, so both a null crmProfileId and any other audit insert failure leave the primary crmColdLead.update intact. Both changes tagged with `audit v12 HIGH` comment.

Added a direct SSE listener in OpportunityComments that opens its own EventSource to /api/events and listens for data.invalidate events. When the DELETE route publishes data.invalidate with queryKeys [["comments", oppId]], the listener now triggers an immediate re-fetch via a stable loadRef, so Rep B sees the deletion instantly instead of waiting up to 30 seconds for the next poll cycle. A loadRef (useRef) was added to give the SSE effect a stable reference to the load function without creating a circular dependency that would cause the SSE connection to be torn down and re-opened on every render. The pre-existing TypeScript errors in src/app/api/saved-views/route.ts (unrelated to this change) were already present before this fix.

Fixed the optimistic/poll race that produced two React rows with the same id. At line 383-384 (the POST-resolution setComments call), added a .filter step that removes any row whose id already equals data.comment.id — except the optimistic placeholder itself (which is about to be swapped). This prevents the scenario where a background poll inserts the canonical row while the POST is still in-flight, and the subsequent map then turns the still-present optimistic row into a second copy of the same canonical id.

Added an ADMIN role gate in the POST handler before accepting visibility=EVERYONE. Any caller whose session.user.crmRole is not 'ADMIN' now receives a 403 when they attempt to create a dashboard with EVERYONE visibility, preventing a REP from broadcasting a dashboard to every CRM user's feed. A clarifying comment was also added noting that SPECIFIC sharedWithIds are already scoped to active CRM profiles via the existing resolveShareTargets call. The change is tagged with a comment referencing audit v12 HIGH #34.

Replaced POST's cross-module `isAdmin` OR (lines 101-105) with the same per-scope `isModuleAdmin` block that PATCH uses. The old code allowed any module admin (e.g. partners-admin) to set `isShared=true` for scopes owned by a different module (e.g. crm-opportunities). The new code derives `isModuleAdmin` from only the module that owns the requested scope — crm requires `crmRole === "ADMIN"`, hr requires `hrRoles` includes `super_admin`, partners requires the user has no `partnerId`. A platform-level `super_admin` (hr role) still spans all modules. An explicit 403 is returned early if `isShared=true` is requested without the right role. Change tagged with `// SECURITY (audit v12 HIGH #35)`.

Applied boundedJson size cap to POST createSchema in src/app/api/saved-views/route.ts. Added a local `boundedJson` validator (mirrors the one in [id]/route.ts) that rejects any single field exceeding 8 KB serialised, and wired it to the `filters`, `sort`, and `columns` fields in `createSchema`. Also added a 32 KB total-body ceiling check in the POST handler — the request text is read via `req.text()` before parsing, and a 413 is returned if the raw length exceeds 32 768 bytes. Both changes are tagged with comment referencing audit v12 HIGH #36.

Added a 'tasks' branch to moduleForScope so scopes like 'tasks:my:mine' and 'tasks:entity:*' return "tasks" instead of null (which previously caused an unconditional 403). Both the GET and POST module-gate conditions were updated to skip the modules-array membership check when module === "tasks", since tasks are available to every authenticated user. The fix is tagged with 'audit v12 HIGH' comments in the source.

Applied safeLabel to all string-typed data cell assignments in the opportunity loop (cells 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 — customerCompanyName, serviceName, stage, customerContactPhone, leadSource, quality/priority, dealType, owner fullName). Moved the safeLabel function definition to before the data-row loop so it is in scope for both the opportunity rows and the pivot header section. All previously-raw string fields that could contain user-supplied formula prefixes (=, +, -, @) are now sanitized. Numeric cells (3, 4, 11) are unaffected as they always hold Number values. Comments reference audit v12 HIGH.

Fixed wonValueEGP permanently being 0 in the sales-report KPI tile. The loss-analytics route was using db.crmOpportunity.count() for WON opportunities which only returned a count, never summing estimatedValueEGP. Replaced it with db.crmOpportunity.aggregate() using both _count._all and _sum.estimatedValueEGP, then added wonValueEGP to the totals response object. The client at client.tsx:114 already reads loss?.totals?.wonValueEGP so no client change was needed.

Added zod validation for startDate and endDate query parameters in the GET handler of src/app/api/audit-logs/route.ts. A `dateStringSchema` using `z.string().refine(...)` validates that each date param is a parseable ISO date string matching `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`. Both params are validated via `safeParse` before any `new Date()` calls or Prisma queries; on failure, the handler returns HTTP 400 with field-level error details instead of allowing Invalid Date to propagate to Prisma and cause a 500. The fix is tagged with the comment `// audit v12 HIGH`. The only TypeScript error present (`src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts`) is pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

Fixed: The `crmAlertRuleFire.create` suppression row was written unconditionally after the channel-dispatch block, even when no notification was actually delivered (e.g. channels=['slack'] with no adapter, or targetUserId null). Introduced a `delivered` boolean flag set to `true` only inside the successful `in-app` branch; the `crmAlertRuleFire.create` call and `fired` increment are now guarded by `if (delivered)`. This ensures the suppression row is only recorded when a real notification went out, preventing entities from being silently and permanently skipped on subsequent cron ticks. Both changes are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.

Added a Zod `.refine()` to `patchSchema` (lines 32-44) that rejects any PATCH request that supplies `scope` without also supplying `predicateJson`. This prevents re-purposing a rule to a different scope while leaving a stale predicate that silently never fires because its field names don't exist on the new scope's entities. The comment references audit v12 HIGH-44.

Fixed REP role-scope bypass in getCalls: the `repId` field has been removed from the `CallFilters` type and the code block that unconditionally wrote `where.callerId = filters.repId` (overriding the scope set by `scopeCallByRole`) has been eliminated. For REP role, `scopeCallByRole` returns `{ callerId: session.id }`; previously any caller could append `?repId=<other-rep>` to overwrite that scope and read another rep's full call history. The fix was applied via the edit to actions.ts (lines 131-163); the linter reformatted the file, confirming the final state: `CallFilters` no longer has a `repId` field, and no code path can override the role-scoped `callerId` filter. The API route at `src/app/api/crm/calls/route.ts` also does not forward any `repId` query parameter to `getCalls`. The two

Fixed: Removed `status` field from `createSchema` (line 25) so clients can no longer supply a status value in the POST body. Hardcoded `status: "PENDING_APPROVAL"` in the `db.crmMeeting.create` call (was `data.status ?? "PENDING_APPROVAL"`), eliminating the path where a REP could POST `{status:'APPROVED'}` and create a meeting that skips the assistant approval queue with `approvedById` left null. Both changes are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.

Fixed the concurrent meeting code collision by moving code generation inside an advisory-locked transaction. The standalone `generateCode()` function (which ran outside any transaction) was removed from `route.ts`. A new exported `generateMeetingCodeInTx(tx)` function was added to `auto-code.ts`; it acquires `pg_advisory_xact_lock(7141003)` and then queries `crmMeeting.findFirst` — all within the caller's transaction. In `route.ts` the plain `generateCode()` call followed by `db.crmMeeting.create()` was replaced with a `db.$transaction` block that calls `generateMeetingCodeInTx(tx)` and then `tx.crmMeeting.create()` in the same transaction boundary. This serialises concurrent creates: the second caller's SELECT only runs after the first caller's INSERT commits, eliminating the P2002 @uniqu

Applied PII mask to the per-id GET handler in the meetings [id] route. After fetching the full meeting record, non-scheduler non-manager callers (e.g. approvers) now have contactPhone, contactName, customerNeed, notes, and deniedReason nulled out before the response is sent — matching the exact mask already applied by the list endpoint. The `isManager` helper already present in the file is reused to grant full visibility to MANAGER/ADMIN/super_admin roles.

Fixed the manager booking bypass that allowed cross-owner opportunity attachment. The oppOwnerCheck query previously used `...(isManager ? {} : { ownerId: scheduledById })`, spreading an empty object for managers and skipping the ownership constraint entirely. A manager could POST {scheduledById: repA, opportunityId: repB_opp} and bind repA's meeting to repB's deal. The fix removes the conditional bypass and enforces `ownerId: scheduledById` unconditionally for all callers, tagged with audit v12 HIGH comment.

Applied audit v12 HIGH fix: added canAccessCompany check to block cross-company OT approvals, and added a team_lead subordinate-chain check using getSubordinateEmployeeIds so a team_lead can only approve OT for employees in their own report hierarchy. Also updated the permission gate from isHROrAdmin to can(authUser, 'overtime:approve') so that team_lead role is correctly admitted by the unified permission table.

Added company-scope filter to Incidents GET handler. Non-super_admin privileged users (hr_manager, accountant, ceo) now have `where.employee.companyId = { in: authUser.companies }` applied automatically (mirroring the bonuses pattern). The `?company=` query parameter is now intersected with the user's allowed company set — if the requested company is not in the user's allowed list, an empty array is returned; super_admins bypass this restriction. Tagged with audit v12 HIGH comment.

Added cross-company authorization gate in the incident POST handler. After looking up the employee, a call to `canAccessCompany(authUser, employee.companyId)` now blocks HR managers from filing incidents against employees at companies they do not have access to, returning HTTP 403. Also added `canAccessCompany` to the import from `@/lib/hr/permissions`. The audit v12 HIGH comment tags the new guard. The single TSC error reported (`src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts:5`) is pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

Added company-scope filter for non-super_admin users who have canViewAllEmployees permission (accountant, ceo, hr_manager). Previously, when canViewAllEmployees returned true, no companyId restriction was applied, allowing cross-tenant leakage of employee records including salary, nationalId, and IBAN. The fix adds an else-if branch: when the user has view-all permission but is NOT super_admin, where.companyId is scoped to { in: authUser.companies } (unless the caller already narrowed to a specific company via the query param). Also added isSuperAdmin to the permissions import.

Fixed the silent account-hijacking vulnerability in the employee create endpoint. When a `work_email` matching an existing User account was supplied, the code now returns HTTP 409 with a descriptive error message and rolls back the already-created HrEmployee row, instead of silently binding the existing account (which would flip `hrAccess=true` and reassign `HrEmployee.userId` to the existing user without consent). The guard was inserted at line 195 of the file, tagged with `audit v12 HIGH`, before the `if (!existingUser)` branch that creates a fresh linked account.

Tightened offenseSchema.deduction_pct in incident.ts to enforce min(0) and max(100) for both number and string union branches, preventing hr_manager from saving negative or >100% deduction percentages. Tagged with audit v12 HIGH comment. The route.ts file already uses createViolationRuleSchema via safeParse so it benefits automatically. One pre-existing unrelated TSC error exists in src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts (evalPredicate not exported from CRM engine) — not introduced by this change.

Fixed PATCH cross-company gate in the HR bonuses route. The handler now fetches the existing bonus record and validates that the authenticated user can access its current company before processing any update. When `data.employee` is supplied (bonus reassignment), it additionally looks up the target employee and calls `canAccessCompany(authUser, targetEmployee.companyId)`, returning 403 if the caller does not have access to the target employee's company. The `employeeId` field is now only written after both checks pass. `canAccessCompany` was added to the import from `@/lib/hr/permissions`. Both guard blocks are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.

Added a status guard in the PATCH handler (lines 85-113) that fetches the current leave request status before applying any field updates. If the request is already 'approved' or 'denied' and the PATCH body includes any of start_date, end_date, leave_type, or days_count, the handler now returns HTTP 409 with a clear message instructing the caller to revoke and re-create. This prevents the orphaned-attendance-log scenario where approved leave days (e.g. 20-24) would retain their 'leave' status while the newly patched range (e.g. 27-31) has no 'leave' rows at all. Status-only and reason-only edits on finalised requests are still allowed. The pre-existing TypeScript error in src/app/api/cron/alert-rules/route.ts (unrelated module export issue) was already present before this change; no errors

Replaced the plain `prisma.hrLeaveRequest.update` in the deny route with `updateMany({ where: { id: pk, status: 'pending' }, ... })`. When two concurrent deny requests race through the read-check together, only the first will match the `status: 'pending'` predicate and get count=1; the second gets count=0 and receives a 409, preventing the double-fire of the "Leave Request Denied" notification. The change is tagged with an `// audit v12 HIGH` comment at lines 35-36 of the modified file.

Added cross-company authorization gate to both the leave-approve and leave-deny routes. After the leave request is fetched from the database, a call to `canAccessCompany(authUser, lr.employee.companyId)` now guards both handlers. An HR manager whose companies list does not include the employee's company receives a 403 before any status mutation or attendance log write can occur. The import of `canAccessCompany` was added to both files. Changes are tagged with `// audit v12 HIGH` comments.
